description: WordPress is the world's most popular open-source CMS, making it a massive target for attackers.
real_world_incidents: Countless mass-compromises of WordPress sites due to vulnerable third-party plugins (e.g., TimThumb, Revolution Slider).
recommended_actions: Keep core, plugins, and themes updated.

audience_guidance.student: WordPress powers much of the web. Because it's so popular, hackers constantly look for weaknesses in its plugins.
audience_guidance.developer: Implement auto-updates, avoid abandoned plugins, and restrict access to the wp-admin directory.
audience_guidance.bug_bounty_hunter: Use wpscan to enumerate plugins, check for exposed xmlrpc.php, and find CVEs for identified plugins.
audience_guidance.pentester: Focus heavily on third-party plugin vulnerabilities rather than WordPress core. Exploit plugins for shell access.
audience_guidance.security_team: Implement a WAF to block common WordPress attacks and strictly manage the plugin inventory.
